observation.visible_scene: A wide beach at sunset (or sunrise) under a sky streaked with orange, pink and blue clouds. The sun sits low on the horizon, casting a bright glow. In the middle distance a line of surf breaks, and the foreground is wet sand acting as a mirror, reflecting warm gold on the left and cool teal on the right.
visible_changes: The breaking wave in the mid-ground undulates slowly: its white foam crest shifts slightly in height and position from frame to frame, indicating continuous wave motion rather than a single event.

The thin sheet of wash water on the foreground sand changes shape across the clip; its curved edge on the right retreats/advances gradually, altering the boundary between the gold-reflecting wet zone and the teal-reflecting zone.
The reflections in the wet foreground shimmer and reorganize subtly as the water surface moves.
The sky, cloud shapes, horizon line and the position of the sun glow remain essentially fixed throughout, showing no camera pan or zoom.
outside_clip_unknowns: Whether the observed surf is the advance or the backwash of a larger swell cycle that began before or continues after this segment.
The cause of the water motion (wind, tide, swell) is not visible.
Any motion of the clouds over a longer timescale is outside this short excerpt.
uncertain_details: The exact direction (shoreward vs seaward) of the foreground wash edge is subtle and hard to fix definitively.
Camera motion cannot be ruled out entirely, but the unchanged sky/horizon strongly suggests a static shot.
The mid-ground wave line moves only slightly between consecutive frames, so its motion is slow and continuous rather than a discrete breaking event.
